evidence: Receiving DO2 at 52.0 h = 12.03 mg/L (online sensor), far above 2.0 mg/L minimum; historical minimum ~9.3 mg/L near t=24 h
Receiving P assay: 0.977 g/L at 36 h, 2.843 g/L at 48 h (available at 52 h), matching source batches (2.98-3.06 g/L at 48 h) within ~5%
Receiving DO2 trajectory (drop ~24 h, recovery ~28 h, ~12-13 plateau) matches the three source batch patterns
Source batches peak at P ~8.0-8.4 g/L at 72 h then slightly decline; receiving is on a similar course with slight lag
Steep product slope (0.98 -> 2.84 g/L over 12 h) argues against feed reduction or stop
submission.rationale: No intervention needed. DO2 is ~12 mg/L with 6x margin above the 2.0 mg/L constraint, product titer (2.84 g/L at 48 h) matches the source calibration envelope within ~5%, and the DO2 trajectory reproduces the healthy source pattern. Interventions would either cut product mass during the steepest production phase or add unneeded aeration; KEEP preserves full productivity and retains all product mass.
submission.uncertainty: Receiving lags sources by roughly half a step in the DO2 pattern, so the final peak may occur slightly later (~76 h) and be a few percent lower; hidden kinetic parameters could alter this. However, no evidence of oxygen limitation, stall, or byproduct degradation exists, and assay noise (~0.02 g/L early) is negligible at current titers. An extra assay was declined because the 48 h assay plus online DO2 already give sufficient confidence.
